headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from Chatwoot’s broad egress into a non-networked data-engineering pair; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty stays moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and send them through integrations, while data-engineering-zoomcamp has no documented I/O surfaces. No shared channel is documented, so a direct injection path is not proven. The plausible risk is limited to manual copy/paste or ad hoc export/import, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies Chatwoot conversation text into the data-engineering-zoomcamp workflow, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of untrusted Chatwoot content into downstream prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from imported text.
Keep the two agents on separate workspaces.
Add a manual review step before any Chatwoot text is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, but the zoomcamp profile shows no data classes touched and no egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, leakage is plausible only through operator-mediated transfer, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is exported into the zoomcamp environment, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are placed under the same shared workspace, files may cross-contaminate.
mitigations: Do not place Chatwoot exports in the zoomcamp workspace.
Redact customer identifiers before any transfer.
Use separate OS accounts for each agent.
Review outbound integrations on Chatwoot before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the container or VM level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but the zoomcamp profile shows network egress none and no write surfaces or mutable shared resources. Without overlapping write or OAuth scopes, the pairwise capability-conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp environment is extended with write access to the same mutable resource as Chatwoot, conflict risk would emerge.
IF shared OAuth scopes are later granted to both agents, overlapping writes could occur.
mitigations: Keep the zoomcamp agent read-only.
Avoid granting shared credentials.
Do not connect both agents to the same mutable database.
Document any future shared resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing reports and integrate with external systems, while the zoomcamp agent has no documented verification or critique surface. If Chatwoot output is reused as input to the zoomcamp workflow, the second agent may treat it as authoritative by default. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is fed into the zoomcamp workflow without a verification step, errors can cascade.
IF the zoomcamp agent is used to generate downstream artifacts from Chatwoot text, it may propagate mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations for any reused Chatwoot-derived facts.
Limit the zoomcamp agent to formatting only.
Flag all Chatwoot-derived inputs as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data and messages, which can include regulated personal data, while the zoomcamp profile has no documented compliance controls or data handling. Because the pair lacks residency, retention, and certification details, the safest reading is a compliance mismatch risk rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF EU personal data from Chatwoot is transferred into the zoomcamp environment, residency obligations may be implicated.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two environments, compliance drift can occur.
mitigations: Classify Chatwoot data before transfer.
Avoid moving personal data into the zoomcamp environment.
Document retention rules for both systems.
Review whether any regulated data is present before sharing.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
